summary.heading: Current state (as of 8 Nov — not updated for later releases)
summary.text: As of the 8 Nov cutoff, 09:00 CET: growth remains firm, but energy is lifting inflation while firms’ wage and price expectations remain broadly flat. The policy lean is hawkish following the November Bank Rate increase to 4.00%. Own nowcasts (approximate 68% judgment ranges, not calibrated model intervals): Q3 GDP +0.6% q/q (0.45–0.75; BoE staff 0.7% in the November MPR); October CPI 3.7% y/y (3.5–3.9, upside skew); July–September unemployment 4.8% (4.6–5.0); private regular pay 3.0% (2.7–3.3). No approved desk baseline has been established. Independent staff-style assessment, not official Bank of England projections.

nowcast_hint: Own estimates as of 8 November. Intervals are approximate judgment ranges labelled 68%, without validated statistical coverage. September GDP, October CPI and July–September labour data were unpublished at the cutoff.
nowcast_note: GDP bridge: average monthly GDP in Q3 divided by the Q2 average, minus one. CPI calculation: assumed monthly price change applied to the latest index, divided by the prior-year index. Other estimates are judgment, not fitted models. BoE staff Q3 GDP of 0.7% is from the November MPR. A full surprises-versus-consensus table is not available; the desk stated that consensus is unavailable and no surprise versus consensus is inferred.

staff_view.lead: As of 8 Nov: growth remains firm, but energy is lifting inflation while firms’ wage and price expectations remain broadly flat. The policy lean is hawkish following the November rate increase.
bullets: Energy raises near-term inflation and squeezes real household income.
Firms’ own-price and wage expectations remain broadly flat; next year’s pay round is crucial.
Hiring intentions are stable and slightly positive (Decision Maker Panel, October, V).
The Labour Force Survey is noisy; recent unemployment moves should not be over-interpreted.
There is no approved desk baseline, and the consumption, investment, real-trade and productivity nowcast is incomplete in this test report.
staff_view.policy: The policy lean is hawkish following the November Bank Rate increase to 4.00%. The November MPR conditions on a market path of 3.9% in Q4 2026 and 4.9% in Q4 2027; that is a forecast-conditioning assumption, not an MPC commitment. No policy recommendation is made. The difference between the two Taylor-type results illustrates sensitivity to the inflation measure, not a precise policy prescription.
